name: 经济系统
description: Bank accounts and classroom stock market. First domain migrated out of api/modules/**. Adopts three pre-existing tables rather than renaming them, because the table and column names are the JSON contract the frontend reads.

data._adopted_note: All three carry their legacy names because `SELECT *` rows are returned straight through to the frontend: deposit_amount, interest_rate, average_buy_price and the JSON-string trend_history are part of the HTTP contract. Renaming them is a coordinated frontend change, tracked as namespace debt by guardrail G10.
data._known_debt: 1. AUTHORIZATION, closed this round: all twenty `/api/economy` routes were reachable with no credential at all. Anonymous callers could deposit into, withdraw from or trade any student's account (the `students/:studentId/**` family and the `/bank/deposit/:studentId`, `/bank/withdraw/:studentId`, `/stocks/buy|sell/:studentId` aliases), settle interest for every account (`/bank/trigger-interest`, `/bank/interest`) and create/update/delete stock listings (`/teacher/stocks*`). Every route now resolves the caller from the kernel's verified request context via `src/economy.authorization.ts` (401 `未登录或登录已过期` before any validation message; 403 `无权限执行该操作` for a known caller without the role) and the service narrows the subject through the classroom port (`src/economy.service.ts`, the "actor scope" section): asset reads are student-self / linked parent / the student's class teacher / admin, asset WRITES are student-self only, class boards are the class's teacher and students, interest settlement is admin/superadmin, and stock CRUD is the owning teacher or admin. The `auth: "actor"` declarations in `provides.routes` below were aspirational until this round; they are now accurate. 2. The two interest routes are admin-only on purpose: the scheduled settlement path is a direct `EconomyService.triggerInterest()` call, not an HTTP request, so gating the route does not disable the cron. 3. NOT done, deliberately: no `ctx.permissions` capability (e.g. `economy.trade`) is declared - the matrix rules on roles, and capability scoping is a separate round. 4. The money paths still pass `actorId: 0` into `classroom.public`'s credit/ledger operations, exactly as the pre-migration code did; the actor is now known at the boundary, so threading it through is a separate reviewable change rather than part of a guard-only batch.
